title: How to Keep a Clear Record of Money You Lend and Borrow
excerpt: Record who paid, how much is outstanding and when you agreed to review or repay it.
introduction: A clear written record helps both people remember what they agreed. This guide covers simple record-keeping, not contract terms or legal rights. Its fictional examples use PKR.
author: Hisabki Kitab Editorial Team

faqs.question: What should a loan record include?
faqs.answer: Record the people involved, original amount, dates, payments, current outstanding amount and what repayment arrangement both people confirmed.

faqs.question: Does a personal note replace a formal agreement?
faqs.answer: A personal record helps with bookkeeping but is not a substitute for a formal agreement or qualified legal advice where those are needed.

sources.title: CFPB: Your Money, Your Goals toolkit

blocks.text: A verbal promise can be remembered differently later, especially when small repayments happen over several months.
Write down the original amount, date, people involved and repayment dates you both agreed. Record each payment separately, then update the balance. Confirm the record together and keep it private.
A fictional record shows PKR 12,000 lent on 1 September. The parties agreed to review payments monthly. The borrower later pays PKR 3,000, which both confirm.
PKR 12,000 original amount - PKR 3,000 confirmed repayment = PKR 9,000 outstanding in this example.

items: Ask whether the other person is comfortable discussing and recording the arrangement.
Write down the original amount, date, payer, recipient and agreed review or payment dates.
Share a copy and ask the other person to confirm it is accurate.
Record each payment once, with its date and amount.
Check the updated balance together if either person has a question.
Counting a promised payment as received before it arrives.
Changing the balance without showing which payment changed it.
Assuming people remember informal changes to the original agreement.

blocks.text: Use a neutral reminder and agree in advance how you will handle a late or missed payment. Consider your own budget before lending money you may need soon.
A shared, up-to-date record can reduce confusion. Keep expectations respectful and seek qualified legal help if a dispute or formal agreement requires it.
